case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to St. Joseph first**, with Muskegon as the backup. My estimated pier ratings for this week: St. Joseph 2, Muskegon 2, Grand Haven 1, South Haven 1 (0-4 scale, average is 2).
- **Expect the pier to be weaker than a boat.** Fish were reported well offshore, so a pier angler will likely need long casts or a wait for the fish to move in.
- **If you can, fish early or late in low light.** Glow spoons and meat rigs were the lures that worked best in the latest reports.
- **Check the water before you go.** The pierhead water and wind data I'd need were unavailable, so confirm there is no sharp temperature drop or strong north or east wind.

## Why

- **St. Joseph and Muskegon lead:** the Aug 3 report rated boats good at both (St. Joseph, 2022-08-03; Muskegon, 2022-08-03), while Grand Haven was average and South Haven slow.
- **I'd expect the pier to trail the boat:** the Aug 3 boat fish were 65 to 140 feet down in 100 to 250 feet of water, which is far from most piers.
- **Low light matters:** the Aug 3 Grand Haven and Muskegon reports both say glow spoons or the bite worked well in low light.
- **Warm water is a caution:** the buoy surface was about 76 F, above the 52-58 F range that Chinook prefer, so I'd expect the fish to stay deep unless a cold upwelling moves in.

## Evidence

**Recent reports** (newest is 2022-08-03, six days old; all are boat reports, and none of the last four weeks has a pier report):
- St. Joseph, 2022-08-03: "Salmon fishing was good… Meat rigs and spoons were catching most of these fish." Water 100+ ft, quality 3.
- Muskegon, 2022-08-03: "Boat anglers were finding salmon 65 to 130 feet down in 140 to 250 feet of water." Quality 3, with glow spoons, meat rigs and green or white flies working.
- Grand Haven, 2022-08-03: "Boat anglers found the salmon action to be fair in 120 to 220 feet of water." Quality 2, with green flies and meat rigs at 65 to 140 ft down.
- South Haven, 2022-08-03: "Salmon fishing was on the slow side but there were a few fish caught." Quality 1, best water around 100 ft.
- Earlier, Jul 14 reports at Grand Haven and Muskegon were slow (quality 0), and St. Joseph on Jul 20 was below average (quality 1). So the trend has been improving.

**Past seasons** (history, not current): the similar-temperature search found only the Aug 3 week itself, so I have no earlier-year matches for water this warm.

**Conditions now:** the live buoy and pier data were unavailable, so I only have the backtest summary for the week before Aug 9. Buoy surface was 76 F at all four ports, up 1 F over the week. I have no pierhead water temperature, no cold-layer depth, and no wind forecast, so I can't say whether an upwelling is under way.

## Caveats

- The newest report is six days old, and the reports are weekly, so the picture may already have shifted.
- The pier ratings are my estimates from boat reports. No pier salmon report appears in the last four weeks.
- The lake model (LMHOFS) pierhead water and wind forecast were unavailable, so I couldn't check for upwelling or wind, which matter most for pier fishing.
- Surface water of 76 F is well above the 52-58 F range general guidance gives for Chinook, so fish will likely be deeper than the surface.

## Sources

- Michigan DNR weekly report, Aug 3, 2022: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3268d0b
- Michigan DNR weekly report, Jul 20, 2022 (St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/323f6bf
- Michigan DNR weekly report, Jul 14, 2022: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/321350c
